correctness.rationale: After diagonalizing Z orthogonally, extract the coefficient of t²su in det(tA+sZ+uI). Fixing the two complementary diagonal rows for sZ and uI leaves the two-by-two principal minor of A; the polarization coefficient is 12. With complementary pair sums w_ij this gives the diagonal block W/24, where W has those off-diagonal entries and zero diagonal, and six independent scalar terms −w_ij a_ij²/12. W is nonzero for Z≠0 and has trace zero, so has a strictly positive eigenvalue; a negative w_ij adds a second independent positive direction. For W entrywise nonnegative the largest eigenvalue bounds every eigenvalue in absolute value (apply |xᵀWx|≤|x|ᵀW|x|). Thus if there are two positive eigenvalues, the remaining two are strictly negative by zero trace. The determinant is then positive; with exactly one positive eigenvalue it is nonpositive, including zeros. Independently, set u₁=λ₁λ₂+λ₃λ₄ and take u₂,u₃ from the other two pair partitions. The three complementary products of W-entries are P_i=e₂−u_i, and the determinant expansion is (∑P_i)²−4∑_{i<j}P_iP_j=−4∑_{i<j}u_iu_j using ∑u_i=e₂. The last sum contains exactly the twelve monomials of e₁e₃ other than the four copies of e₄. This proves the determinant criterion including all equalities. Orthogonal decomposition along any vector of strictly positive quadratic value proves the reverse inequality; zero gives it trivially, and PSD arguments have nonnegative value by the weighted principal-minor formula. I checked that (−1,3,4,100) gives e₁e₃−4e₄=56528 outside the weak balance cone, and that (−1,1,2,3) gives −1 and the asserted deficit −5t²/144 for the given positive definite matrices. The frozen symbolic support was inspected, not executed.

originality.rationale: The principal-minor identity, strict pair-sum positivity test on definite inputs, and strict and weak spectral-balance sufficiency are established antecedents. The distinct contribution is the exact positive-index-one criterion on the full ten-dimensional space, including the polynomial equality boundary and parameters outside weak spectral balance. The comparison in the frozen record would be more complete if it also cited the weak-balance result in Theorem 4.7 and its proof; that result still does not give the necessary-and-sufficient boundary.

value.rationale: For a natural signed Alexandrov–Fenchel quadratic form this replaces a sufficient cone with a checkable necessary-and-sufficient spectral boundary on the full space, rather than only positive input tests. It handles degenerate forms and exhibits both a signed case that works outside prior balance and a positive-definite inequality failure when only the pair-sum test holds. These distinctions are substantive even though the classification is specific to dimension four and one signed reference.
